tierReason: graphs/basics-spawn-by-species.json (a string attribute chosen per point feeding the spawner's asset attribute) and graphs/basics-quota-rebalance.json (holding a population to a stated mix), plus the shape/disc and write/instances-by-species primitives, all ship in the installed package and together are a near-solution; the stated 60/30/10 mix is not reachable with the four-entry primitive as-is.
title: A round grove of about 1500 trees, 60% oak, 30% birch, 10% pine, mixed through each other

checks.description: The grove output holds between 1300 and 1700 instances inclusive (the brief's 'about 1500'). Instances that cannot be read on the CPU (device residency) fail every check.
The instances carry exactly the asset ids oak, birch and pine: all three present, no other id.

Shares are taken over the oak, birch and pine instances only (any other id is ignored here and fails species-ids instead); each named kind's share is within 5 percentage points of its target, inclusive with 1e-9 float slack: oak 60%, birch 30%, pine 10%. No named instance at all fails.
Every tree stands within 50 m of the origin measured across the ground (XZ), with 0.01 m tolerance (plus 1e-9 slack); a non-finite position counts as outside.

Over every unordered pair of trees standing within 5 m of each other across the ground (XZ), the percentage of same-kind pairs exceeds chance for the grove's own mix (the sum over ALL asset ids present of the squared share of all instances) by at most 4 percentage points, inclusive with 1e-9 slack. Fails when no such pair exists, when there are more than 200000 trees, or when more than 5000000 pairs are found (trees piled together). Non-finite positions are skipped.

The trees fill the whole 50 m circle: at least 44% of the trees (inclusive, 1e-9 slack) stand more than 35 m from the origin across the ground, AND every 10 m x 10 m square with edges on multiples of 10 m that lies wholly inside the circle (its farthest corner within 50 m) holds at least one tree.
